slice-tier.title: Which builder tier builds this work item

question.instructions: Pick the smallest builder tier that can build this work item. The state is how much the work item holds and whether that fits each tier's sizing limits.

criteria.small: A haiku-class builder. The work item fits the small limits.
criteria.medium: A mid-size builder. The work item fits the medium limits.
criteria.large: The largest builder. The work item is bigger than the medium limits.

inputs.work-item.criteria: acceptance criteria in the work item
inputs.work-item.files: distinct paths the work item names
inputs.work-item.words: words in the body outside headings
inputs.work-item.fits_small: whether it is within the small tier's limits
inputs.work-item.fits_medium: whether it is within the medium tier's limits

understand.title: Is this ask understood well enough to build

question.instructions: A person asked for a change, and the ask is a work item whose source names what they said and who said it. The factory asks this before it builds the item. The state is the work item: its title and state, the person's words, who asked and where, and any acceptance criteria it has so far. Pick what happens next.

criteria.proceed: The ask is clear enough to build. The work item opens, and the factory builds it under its lease, writing its plan as acceptance criteria first.
criteria.redraft: What the person wants is clear, but the work item does not say it well. Someone rewrites the item, which asks this point again, before anything is built.
criteria.ask: The ask is unclear. Someone asks the person who made it what they mean before anything is built.
criteria.refuse: The ask will not be built. The work item is dropped, with the reason.

inputs.work-item.state: the work item's state: proposed for an ask nobody has kept yet
inputs.work-item.title: the work item's title
inputs.work-item.source.ask.via: where the ask came in, such as hud, shell or mcp
inputs.work-item.acceptance: the acceptance criteria the item has so far

rows.note: A person opened the item already, or it did not start as a proposal.

ship-skip.title: May this release skip the human gate

question.instructions: May this release pass the ship gate without a person approving it? The state is what the release would change. No model decider answers this point, since a model's answer may route or report and never authorizes a release.

criteria.true: An agent may pass the gate for this release.
criteria.false: A person approves the release at the gate.

inputs.release.files_changed: files changed since the serving release
inputs.release.app_changed: whether any file under the app directory changed

rows.note: Never, until someone adds a row above this one that says when.

deciders.note: The ship gate's quorum: a gate that asks this point takes its approver count from here.

finding-triage.title: What to do about this finding

question.instructions: A finding from chant workspace graph --intent, or from chant workspace check --changes, is a gap between what the workspace decided and what it holds. Pick what happens to it. The state is the finding and the region it fired on.

criteria.work-item: Someone closes the gap. It becomes a work item whose source names the finding and its region.
criteria.needs-a-decision: The gap is a choice nobody has made. Someone writes a decision before any work starts.
criteria.leave: Nothing happens. The finding is known, accepted or already taken.

inputs.finding.addressed: whether a work item already addresses it
inputs.region.path: the path the finding fired on
inputs.region.member: the member the region is in
inputs.region.generated: whether the region is a generated file

rows.note: A work item already addresses it.
A decided decision that nobody is carrying out is work.
No current decision that everyone agrees with covers the region.

A change crossed a boundary a record draws. Someone decides whether the boundary moves or the change goes, and no model answers leave for it. change-uncovered has no row: whether an uncovered change is work, a decision or nothing depends on what the path is, which the model reads.

needs-a-decision.title: Does this change need a decision

question.instructions: Does the change need a decision written before it lands? The state is the commits in the change's window that changed its region, as chant workspace graph --intent reads them, and the decisions the change's work item implements.

criteria.true: Someone writes a decision that covers the change, or amends one, before it lands.
criteria.false: The decisions already in the workspace cover the change.

inputs.commit.count: commits in the window that changed the region
inputs.commit.undecided: of those, the commits no decision's path window holds
inputs.commit.decided_by_window: of those, the commits in a decision's window that are not that decision's own work
inputs.region.generated: whether the region is a generated file
inputs.work-item.implements: the decisions the change's work item implements

rows.note: Every commit in the window is a decision's own work.

question.instructions: An intent walk (chant workspace graph --intent) asks this at a commit no decision's window holds: was the change meant to carry out a decision? The state is the region walked and the commit's node.

criteria.carried-out-decision: The change carried out a decision, written down or not.
criteria.incidental: The change was incidental: a fix, a rename or upkeep that no decision is about.
criteria.unknown: The person walking the region does not know.

inputs.region.id: the region walked, as graph --intent names it: region:<path>, with :<start>-<end> or #<symbol>
inputs.node.id: the node of the walk the question is asked at, as graph --intent names it

deciders.note: The person walking the region answers. No table or model answers for them.

intent-judgment.title: What the gap between this decision and the code is

question.instructions: An intent walk asks this at a decision, or at a commit made inside a decision's window that is not the decision's own work: does the code do what the decision says, and if not, why? The state is the region walked and the node.

criteria.drift: Drift: the code moved away from a decision that still holds.
criteria.unwritten-supersession: A decision nobody wrote down superseded it.
criteria.decision-wrong: The decision was wrong, and is reopened.
criteria.no-gap: There is no gap: the code does what the decision says.
criteria.not-decidable: It can't be decided from this walk.

inputs.region.id: the region walked, as graph --intent names it: region:<path>, with :<start>-<end> or #<symbol>
inputs.node.id: the node of the walk the question is asked at, as graph --intent names it

deciders.note: The person walking the region answers. No table or model answers for them.

question.instructions: An intent walk asks this at any other node, such as a unit, contract, evidence, artifact or the region itself: what was done about the question the walk asks there? The state is the region walked and the node.

criteria.handled: Handled: it is done, or nothing needed doing.
criteria.skipped: Skipped, and the note says why.
criteria.needs-discussion: It needs a discussion or a decision first.

inputs.region.id: the region walked, as graph --intent names it: region:<path>, with :<start>-<end> or #<symbol>
inputs.node.id: the node of the walk the question is asked at, as graph --intent names it

deciders.note: The person walking the region answers. No table or model answers for them.

agent-question.title: A question an agent asked the people working with it

question.instructions: An agent asked the people working with it this question, with options of its own, and acts on the one they pick. The question and its options come with each ask, as hud's hud_ask and AskUserQuestion give them.

inputs.ask.id: the asker's own id for this ask, such as hud's request id for the question, so each ask is a question of its own
inputs.ask.by: who asked: the agent, or the session it asked in

deciders.note: A person in the room answers. No table or model answers an agent's question for them.
